content: Hydrocortisone ointment is an anti-inflammatory medication approved by the FDA for the treatment of itching associated with minor skin irritations and rashes. These conditions may include eczema, insect bites, reactions to soaps and detergents, cosmetics, jewelry, seborrheic dermatitis, psoriasis, and contact with poison ivy, oak, or sumac. It is also used for external genital, feminine, and anal itching. The most common adverse reaction reported is itching. For adults, hydrocortisone ointment should be applied to the affected area no more than three to four times daily for minor skin irritations and rashes. For external anal itching, it is recommended to cleanse the affected area with mild soap and warm water, rinse thoroughly, and gently dry by patting or blotting with toilet tissue or a soft cloth before applying the product. For pediatric patients aged two years and older, the ointment can be applied to the affected area up to three to four times daily for minor skin irritations and rashes. For children under 12 years of age with external anal itching, a doctor should be consulted before use. Off-label uses of hydrocortisone ointment in both adult and pediatric populations are not well-documented, and there is limited information available regarding such uses. There is no specific information in the drug label regarding contraindications, warnings, clinical trial experiences, post-marketing experiences, or drug interactions for hydrocortisone ointment. Additionally, there is no FDA guidance on its use during pregnancy, labor and delivery, breastfeeding, or in specific populations such as pediatric, geriatric, gender-specific, racial groups, or patients with renal or hepatic impairment. Similarly, there is no guidance for its use in immunocompromised patients. For administration, the product should not be used if the seal is punctured or missing. To open, reverse the cap to puncture the seal. The ointment should be stored at room temperature, and the lot number and expiration date can be found on the crimp of the tube. If an overdose or drug poisoning is suspected, contact the National Poison Help hotline at 1-800-222-1222 immediately. The mechanism of action, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, and nonclinical toxicology of hydrocortisone ointment are not well-documented in the drug label. Similarly, there is limited information regarding clinical studies, how the product is supplied, and storage instructions. There is no established interaction between alcohol and hydrocortisone ointment. Patients should consult their doctor regarding the effects of alcohol consumption while using this medication.
